title: Edmund and the Cipher
premise: Jude Voss, coroner of the fading town of Harrow Bend, receives a letter confessing to a murder — signed by Edmund Hale, the man whose autopsy Jude performed three weeks earlier. The confession is written in a cipher Edmund used as a boy, and it points to a second body no one ever found: the town's beloved founding matriarch, declared dead by accident in 1987. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Jude must decode Edmund's obsession, confront the powerful families who buried the truth, and decide whether exposing it will save or destroy the people they love. In the end, Jude finds the hidden grave, proves the murder, and chooses duty over the quiet life they'd built — turning the evidence over even though it implicates their own late mentor.
about_author: Yara Voss is the pen name of a former rural journalist who spent a decade covering small-town courtrooms and unmarked cemeteries across the American Midwest. They write mysteries about the secrets communities keep to survive themselves.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Three weeks after signing off on Edmund Hale's autopsy, Jude receives a letter postmarked the day after his funeral: a full confession to a murder, written partly in cipher. The emotional beat is cold dread — the dead don't mail letters, and someone wants Jude to know it.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishing Harrow Bend: its cemetery rows, its feuds, and Edmund, the reclusive retired schoolteacher who taught half the town their letters. Jude rereads the old file on the 1987 death of matriarch Cordelia Ashcombe, ruled accidental. Beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Loved Codes
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Visiting Edmund's sealed house, Jude finds childhood cipher notebooks and a photograph of young Edmund with Cordelia — and a torn corner matching something missing from her case file. Beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: What the Family Swore
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Marian Ashcombe, Cordelia's imperious granddaughter, learns Jude has reopened boxes. She warns Jude off with velvet menace, invoking the town's dependence on Ashcombe money. Beat: power flexing quietly, corruption wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The county attorney confirms the homicide clock expires in ninety days; after that, the truth dies legally forever. Jude's deputy friend Ray begs them to let sleeping dogs lie. Beat: the weight of the deadline and the first real cost of pursuing it.

chapters.title: First Key
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Decoding begins: the cipher keys off hymn numbers from the church where Edmund taught Sunday school. The first decrypted passage names a place — the flooded quarry — and a date two days before Cordelia's 'accident.' Beat: grim exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Quarry in Winter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Dredging permits stall; someone upstream is blocking them. Jude meets Delia Moss, an archivist who knew Edmund, and feels an unexpected warmth she distrusts. Beat: love beginning against Jude's better judgment.

chapters.title: A Death Ruled Kindly
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Flashback chapter through archives: 1987, the young coroner — Jude's mentor, Walt Greer — signs the accidental-death ruling in under a day. Delia finds his margin note: 'Edmund saw. Deal with him gently.' Beat: horror at a trusted name.

chapters.title: Gently, Then
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts the dying, dementia-shadowed Walt, who alternates between denial and fragments: 'Cordelia asked for it' and 'the family paid for my roof.' Beat: betrayal — the father figure was bought, and Jude owes him everything.

chapters.title: Second Body
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A decoded page reveals Edmund didn't just witness the murder — he helped hide the body, believing for fifty years he was protecting a battered woman's final wish gone wrong. Beat: moral vertigo; the confession is also an accusation of himself.

chapters.title: The Arson at Mill Row
chapters.summary: Marian's POV. Someone burns Edmund's house; Marian ordered surveillance, not fire, but her son took initiative. Her control slips. Beat: corruption compounding — each cover-up demands a worse one.

chapters.title: Ashes and Hymnals
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Sifting the burned house, Jude recovers a fire-scarred cipher wheel and a letter addressed to Delia, revealing Edmund trusted her all along. Ray warns Jude they're next. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Delia's Choice
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia admits she corresponded with Edmund for years and never pushed him to go public — she chose the archive over the living. She and Jude collide over whether truth or safety comes first. Beat: love tested by duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Walt's POV, lucid window. Walt recounts the night in 1987: Cordelia, beaten by her son-in-law, begged Edmund to make it look like an accident so her family would inherit untainted. He did — then couldn't live inside the lie. Beat: tragic sympathy for everyone complicit.

chapters.title: Ninety Becomes Thirty
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The county attorney, now on Ashcombe retainer, moves to seal the case as harassment. Jude loses official standing and goes rogue, copying files to Delia's archive. Beat: isolation — the institution itself is the antagonist.

chapters.title: What Edmund Buried
chapters.summary: Jude and Delia's POV, alternating. Using the wheel and quarry maps, they triangulate a drainage culvert beneath the old Ashcombe orchard. They find remains with a healed fracture matching Cordelia's records. Beat: awe and grief — proof at last.

chapters.title: The Son-in-Law Still Breathing
chapters.summary: Marian's POV. Her father, the actual killer, is senile in a care home; Marian realizes exposure will outlive any statute in reputation alone. She offers Jude money, then threats, then her own version of mercy. Beat: power's last corruptions.

chapters.title: Confession, Countersigned
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude obtains a deathbed statement from Walt reaffirming the cover-up, and matches Edmund's cipher key to handwriting evidence tying the 1987 ruling to coercion. Ray finally stands with them. Beat: the pieces locking into place.

chapters.title: Orchard Night
chapters.summary: Climax. Jude's POV. Marian's son tries to destroy the culvert site with machinery at night; Jude and Delia stand in the path, cameras running, until deputies — tipped by Ray — arrive. Marian arrives too and, seeing witnesses, orders her son to stop. Beat: courage against brute force.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The formal exhumation before the statute expires; forensic confirmation identifies Cordelia Ashcombe, cause: blunt force trauma. Charges are filed against the surviving killer and the estate's enablers. Beat: hard-won vindication, joyless but real.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Edmund is publicly honored and privately mourned; Delia publishes his notebooks intact, guilt and all. She and Jude choose each other without pretending the cost was small. Beat: love that survived duty's demands.

chapters.title: Closing the Book
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue: Jude resigns the coroner's office rather than sign another kindly ruling, and carves Edmund's name beside Cordelia's new stone. Final line of the cipher, decoded at last: 'Tell the truth slowly, and tell it all.' Beat: peace earned, not given.
